reasoning_details.text:
I'm starting fresh on this case with no prior findings or operator instructions to go on, so I need to scan for conflicts myself. I'm noting the delivery endpoint for customer order input, flagged with an unconfirmed contact status for Celia Hollowmere and access needing verification.

Looking at the messages, the customer's initial note said the receiving contact could only accept delivery until early afternoon, but a later correction extended access until 18:00 local time — though it still doesn't clarify who's actually authorized to sign for the delivery. The delivery promise window runs 11:00–16:00 CEST, so while the 18:00 correction doesn't conflict with that window directly, the real unresolved issue is authorization: the named contact can't be confirmed as the one permitted to take custody. I need to check whether this has already been flagged to the customer, since I recall an operator note about waiting until an authorized receiver is identified.

There's also a conflicting availability window: the customer first said early afternoon, then corrected to 18:00 access, while the delivery promise window itself ends at 16:00 CEST — all customer-side statements that don't line up. And there's ambiguity around whether Celia Hollowmere, named as the handoff contact, is actually authorized to inspect/sign, versus the customer's separate claim that the receiving contact can't take delivery after early afternoon — unclear if these refer to the same person. The key finding is to ask the customer directly whether Celia is authorized and what her real availability window is.

Separately, the Munich handoff site is a third-party business whose front desk can't accept custody without the site contact present, which adds another layer of dependency. Tracking data shows the estimated delivery time creeping toward 15:58 CEST — just inside the 16:00 window, but still potentially after the customer's "early afternoon" cutoff, which is worth flagging as a possible scheduling conflict.

The customer's own correction extending the window to 18:00 resolves the timing issue, so the main remaining open question is really about receiver authority at the drop-off site — I don't think I need extra tool calls like checking inbox threads for this, since the case file conversations should already cover it.

I'll consolidate into one finding asking the customer to confirm both whether Celia Hollowmere is authorized to inspect and sign, and the correct access hours given the conflicting statements. The key conflict quotes are the endpoint listing "Celia Hollowmere" as contact versus the customer's own message stating they still cannot confirm who's authorized — I'll pair those as the conflict evidence, with the paying customer (cus-025, "Calverona Auto") as the contact to query. I'll also note the operator's earlier ask for an authorized receiver lapsed without a recorded check-back, so it doesn't count as resolved, and fold the hours confirmation into the same question before writing up the submission.
